_comment: Fixture-only config for the bundled offline test run. Same shape as config.example.json with three differences, each noted below, that suit a six-call sample of abridged transcripts. Do not copy this into ~/.leanscale-gtm/ — copy config.example.json.

dimensions.label: Metrics
dimensions.evidence_rule: A quantified business impact in the buyer's own words — money, time, headcount, volume or a missed deadline. A rep asserting a number does not count unless the buyer confirms it on the call.
dimensions.met_means: A number and what it is a number of. 'Roughly 30 hours a month between two people' is met; 'it takes ages' is missing.

dimensions.label: Economic Buyer
dimensions.evidence_rule: The person who can approve the spend is named, and either their authority or their criteria is stated on the call.
dimensions.met_means: Named plus one of: they are in the room, their approval threshold is stated, or the buyer describes what they will need from them. A job title with no name is partial.

dimensions.label: Decision Criteria
dimensions.evidence_rule: What the buyer will compare options against, or what would disqualify one, stated by the buyer.
dimensions.met_means: At least two criteria, or one criterion plus a disqualifier. A single vague preference is partial.

dimensions.label: Decision Process
dimensions.evidence_rule: The steps, forums and people between today and a signature, stated by the buyer.
dimensions.met_means: A sequence with at least one date or forum. One step with no sequence is partial.

dimensions.label: Paper Process
dimensions.evidence_rule: How a contract actually gets signed: legal review, procurement, security review, required artefacts, typical duration.
dimensions.met_means: At least one concrete constraint with a duration or an artefact. Mark not_applicable on a first discovery call where no evaluation has been agreed.

dimensions.label: Identify Pain
dimensions.evidence_rule: A business consequence the buyer feels, beyond a process complaint — what it costs them, personally or commercially.
dimensions.met_means: The buyer names a consequence, not just an inconvenience. 'It's annoying' is missing; 'I told the board February and I missed it' is met.

dimensions.label: Champion
dimensions.evidence_rule: Someone who sells internally when you are not in the room — evidenced by them taking an action, not by them being friendly.
dimensions.met_means: They commit to do something internally: build the case, make an introduction, take it to a forum. Enthusiasm with no action is partial.

dimensions.label: Competition
dimensions.evidence_rule: What else is being considered, including do-nothing, an in-house build, and competing internal budget priorities.
dimensions.met_means: The alternative is named and something is learned about how the buyer weighs it. Naming a competitor and moving on is partial.

_framework_help: The qualification framework you actually coach to. Built-in sets: MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, BANT, SPICED, CHALLENGER, COMMAND_OF_THE_MESSAGE. Set name to CUSTOM and replace the dimensions array to coach against your own. Every dimension needs a key, a label, a tier ('fundamental' or 'advanced'), an evidence_rule (what counts as proof) and a met_means (where the line between met and partial sits) — those two strings are what the scoring pass reads, so vague ones produce vague coaching.
_call_types_help: Which call types to coach. Anything not in this list is skipped. Common additions: 'technical_validation', 'negotiation', 'qbr', 'renewal'.
_reps_help: The roster being coached. start_date drives tenure-aware coaching — a rep ten weeks in is coached on fundamentals, a rep three years in on the advanced dimensions. email is also how speakers get resolved to internal when a transcript export carries no affiliation flag, so keep it accurate.
_tenure_bands_help: Under ramping_days = ramping; under developing_days = developing; beyond that = tenured. Industry defaults — set them to your own ramp definition if you have one.
_mechanics_targets_help: FIXTURE: question rate lowered from the shipped default of 8 because these sample transcripts are abridged excerpts, not full recordings, so every count is artificially low. Every other threshold is the shipped default.
_competitors_help: Extra competitor names to count mentions of, on top of profile.json's competitors list. Include 'in-house build' style alternatives if your team says them out loud. Mention counting is a plain keyword scan and is reported as a mention count, never as a judgment about how well competition was handled — that judgment is a framework dimension.
_pricing_keywords_help: Words that locate the first pricing moment in a call. This is a locator, not an interpreter — the report says when pricing came up and who raised it, and leaves the meaning to you.
_output_audience_help: 'manager' (default) writes one team pattern report and nothing rep-facing. 'reps' additionally writes a one-page coaching card per rep into coaching/ inside the run folder, so you can hand them out without forwarding the team report. Reps ignore per-call feedback; managers act on patterns — so the team report is the product either way.
_include_per_call_reviews_help: Adds the full per-call scorecards to the end of the report. Off by default: the point of this plugin is one pattern the manager can coach on Monday, not nine call reviews nobody reads. Every per-call score is always in findings.json regardless.
_exemplar_call_ids_help: FIXTURE: the two calls the fictional manager considers good. One of them scores well below the other, which is what makes the calibration section worth looking at.
_transcript_source_help: provider is one of: gong, fireflies, chorus, grain, otter, zoom, google_drive, local_directory, mixed. internal_domains is how a speaker gets resolved to your side when the export carries no affiliation flag — list every domain your team sends mail from. local_directory is used by the local_directory provider; folder_id by google_drive; workspace by the platforms that scope tokens to one.
_window_days_help: How far back to pull calls. 30 suits a monthly cadence; 90 gives a rep with low call volume enough evidence to be coached on.
_min_call_duration_sec_help: Ignore anything shorter — a five-minute call is a reschedule, not a discovery call, and it drags every average down.
_min_calls_per_rep_help: FIXTURE: lowered from 3 because the sample has two calls per rep. In a real deployment leave it at 3.
_min_instances_for_pattern_help: A dimension needs at least this many scored calls before it can be called the team's weakest. Stops a two-call fluke becoming Monday's coaching topic.
_coverage_warn_pct_help: Dimensions below this coverage percentage are listed as secondary gaps under the headline finding.
_material_deal_floor_help: Deal size above which a framework gap is treated as expensive. null inherits profile.json's material_deal_floor, which is what you want unless coaching should use a different bar from the rest of the suite.
_demote_unverified_quotes_help: On (recommended): any met or partial whose supporting quote cannot be found verbatim in the transcript is demoted to unscored and listed as a data-quality finding. This is the guard against a coaching report built on a paraphrase that nobody actually said.
_cadence_help: Documentation only — how often you intend to run this. Nothing here schedules anything; you run it, or your own scheduler does.
